questions.question: Removing barriers or restrictions set by the government is called ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Liberalization**__ is a process whereby a government lifts restrictions on some private individual activities.
 
• Liberalization occurs when something which used to be banned is no longer banned, or when the government regulations are relaxed.
 
• India lifted restrictions and opened up its economy for foreign investors in 1991.

questions.question: In economics, tools, machines, buildings that can be used in production over many years are called ______.
questions.solution:
• **Fixed capital **is capital or money that we invest in fixed assets. In other words, money that we invest in assets of a durable nature. These are assets that we repeatedly use over a long period.
 
• Fixed Capital are tangible assets that we cannot convert into cash easily. Property is an example of a fixed asset. So are plant and equipment.
 
• We do not resell fixed assets as part of our everyday business operations. We use fixed assets in the production of our company’s income or for administrative purposes.
 
• In other words fixed capital are the assets that are used to produce more capital.

questions.question: The lions placed on top of a pillar at Sarnath that we see on our notes were originally carved out on which material?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Ashoka Lion capital or the Sarnath lion capital **__is the national symbol of India is __**made up of stone**__.
 
• The capital has four Asiatic lions—symbolising power, courage, pride and confidence—seated on a circular abacus. The abacus has sculptures of a bull, a horse, a lion and an elephant.
 
• While Buddhist interpretations say the animals represent different phases of the Buddha’s life, non-religious interpretations say they depict the reign of emperor Ashoka in the four geographical directions, while the wheels depict his enlightened rule.
 
• The capital was adopted as the national emblem on January 26, 1950. It was chosen as a symbol of contemporary India’s reaffirmation of its ancient commitment to world peace and goodwill.

questions.question: On which date the longest day and the shortest night of the year occur in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
• 21 June summer solstice marks the longest day and the shortest night of the calendar year and the beginning of summer in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the sun, sunlight falls at a steeper angle on it to cause the hot months of summer. The farther north you live, the longer the hours of daylight around the time of the summer solstice.
 
• When the Sun reaches its highest position in the sky and is the day with the longest period of daylight.

questions.question: The climate of India has broadly been described as of which type?
questions.solution:
• Indian Climate is described as the Monsoon type of climate due to seasonal reversal of winds.
 
• This happens due to the differential heating of land and water bodies and pressure situations.
 
• The monsoon type of climate is based on distinct season.
 
• India is home to an extraordinary variety of climatic regions, ranging from tropical in the south to temperate and alpine in the Himalayan north however, it is broadly believed to be monsoon type climate.

questions.solution:

questions.question: A boat full of iron nails is floating on water in a lake. When the iron nails are removed, the water level ______.
questions.solution:
• When the iron nails are removed the water tends to fall.
 
• It is somewhat related to Archimedes principle.
 
• Archimedes' principle states that the upward buoyant force that is exerted on a body immersed in a fluid, whether fully or partially submerged, is equal to the weight of the fluid that the body displaces and acts in the upward direction at the center of mass of the displaced fluid. So when the nail is removed the level of water decreased.

questions.question: A thermometer is used to measure ______.
questions.solution:
• Thermometre is used to measure temperature not heat.
 
• Thermometers are based on the principal of thermal expansion. When a substance gets hotter, it expands to a greater volume. Nearly all substances exhibit this behavior of thermal expansion.
 
• As the temperature of the liquid in a thermometer increases, its volume increases. The liquid is enclosed in a tall, narrow glass (or plastic) column with a constant cross-sectional area. The increase in volume is thus due to a change in height of the liquid within the column.

questions.question: The large carnivores are also called ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Large Carnivores are Tertiary consumers.**__
 
• An example is a hawk that eats owls. Each food chain end with a top predator, and animal with no natural enemies.
 
• Quaternary consumers are predators who eat a lot of prey but are usually not preyed upon themselves. They are the apex predators at the top of the food chain.

__**Explanation**__-

Consumers are organisms that eat other organisms to obtain energy. There are several types of consumers:

 
• **Herbivores:** These are primary consumers because they are the first, or primary, step on the food chain. They eat producers like plants and algae. Examples include cows, deer, and rabbits.
 
• **Carnivores: **These are secondary or tertiary consumers. They eat other consumers. Carnivores can be further sorted into more specific categories:

 
• **Secondary Consumers: **These eat the primary consumers (herbivores). Examples include snakes (which eat mice) and lions (which eat zebras and gazelles).
 
• **Tertiary Consumers:** These eat secondary consumers. They are typically top predators in their ecosystem. For example, an owl might eat a snake (which has eaten a mouse, which has eaten a plant).

 
• **Omnivores:** These consumers eat both producers (like plants) and consumers (animals). Many humans, bears, and raccoons are omnivores.
 
• **Detritivores:** Detritivores consume decaying organic material, such as leaf litter, dung, and dead bodies, and serves to recycle nutrients back into the food chain. Examples include earthworms and vultures.
 
• **Decomposers:** While decomposers also consume decaying organic material, they do so through a process of breaking it down chemically. Fungi and bacteria are the primary decomposers.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT true with respect to Janani Suraksha Yojana?

options.text: its objective is reducing maternal and infant mortality
it is an intervention under the National Rural Health Mission
it is not a centrally sponsored scheme

questions.solution:
• JSY is a centrally sponsored scheme, which integrates cash assistance with delivery and post-delivery care.
 
• Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission. It is being implemented with the objective of reducing maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women.
 
• The scheme, launched on 12 April 2005 by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, is under implementation in all states and Union Territories (UTs), with a special focus on Low Performing States (LPS).

 
 
• Centrally Sponsored Schemes are the schemes by the centre where there is financial participation by both the centre and states.

questions.question: J. Kepler is famous for the discovery of laws of ______.
questions.solution:
• Johannes Kepler created three laws of **planetary motion.**
 
• The path of the planets about the sun is elliptical in shape, with the center of the sun being located at one focus. (The Law of Ellipses)
 
• An imaginary line drawn from the center of the sun to the center of the planet will sweep out equal areas in equal intervals of time. (The Law of Equal Areas)
 
• The ratio of the squares of the periods of any two planets is equal to the ratio of the cubes of their average distances from the sun. (The Law of Harmonies)

questions.question: Chagos Archipelago dispute is the reason of tension between which two countries?

options.text: United Kingdom and United States of America
Mauritius and United States of America

questions.solution:
• It is a reason of dispute between United Kingdom and Mauritius.
 
• The Chagos Archipelago is a group of seven atolls comprising more than 60 islands in the Indian Ocean about 500 km south of the Maldives.
 
• Before Mauritian independence, in 1965, the UK split the archipelago from the territory of Mauritius to form the British Indian Ocean Territory and permitted the US to use it for defence purposes for 50 years (until December 2016) followed by a 20-year optional extension.
 
• Following this US Military Base was setup in Diego Garcia, the largest of the islands. The UN resolutions banned the dismemberment of colonial territories before independence. Therefore Mauritius claims sovereignty over the islands and states that Britain’s claim is a violation of law and of UN Resolution.

questions.question: India to Thailand highway passes through which country?
questions.solution:
• It passes through Myanmar.
 
• The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway is a highway under construction under India's Look East policy that will connect Moreh, India with Mae Sot, Thailand via Myanmar.
 
• The road is expected to boost trade and commerce in the ASEAN–India Free Trade Area, as well as with the rest of Southeast Asia. India has also proposed extending the highway to Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam.
 
• India and ASEAN have plans to extend this route to Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam as this connectivity will generate annually, an estimated US$70 billion in incremental GDP and 20 million in incremental aggregate employment by 2025, and India has offered US$1 billion line-of-credit for the India-ASEAN connectivity projects
